title: Random Change Ringing as a Shuffle: Does Ringing's One-Place Rule Mix Bells Fast When Swaps Run in Parallel?
target_platform: Exact Markov chain distribution evolution on the symmetric group S_n, n in 4..8 (Python standard library; bounded local CPU)
interest_statement: In change ringing, a bell can only move one place between rows, so a change is a set of disjoint swaps of neighbouring bells. Card-shuffling theory says moves that only swap neighbours mix slowly. I want to know whether doing many neighbour swaps in parallel, as a ringing change does, rescues mixing, and whether it saves total work or only time. Origin: crossing change ringing with shuffling, and taking the parallelism question from bee recruitment (see discovery.md).
hypothesis: Chain C (random change): from rounds (identity), each step applies a uniformly random nonempty set of disjoint adjacent transpositions on n bells. Chain A (baseline): lazy random adjacent transposition (stay with prob 1/2, else swap a uniform adjacent pair). t_X(n) = least t with total variation distance to uniform on S_n <= 0.25. Held-out n in {7,8}: (H1) speedup R(n) = t_A(n)/t_C(n) is larger than R(6) for both n=7 and n=8, and R(8) > R(7); (H2) total expected swaps to mix, t_C(n)*s_C(n), is below t_A(n)*0.5 at both n=7 and n=8, where s_C(n) is the mean swaps per change (parallelism saves work, not just time). (G) Gate: exact evolution conserves probability within 1e-9; the number of nonempty changes equals F(n+1)-1 (Fibonacci); TV is non-increasing in t for chain A; dev n in {4,5,6}.
falsification_criteria: FALSIFIED if gate G passes and H1 or H2 fails at held-out n. CORROBORATED if G passes and both hold. UNASSESSED if G fails or the held-out run does not finish within budget (t cap 5000 steps, 20 min CPU). Dev n in {4,5,6} only; protocol.md, evaluate_ringing.py and freeze.json are hash-frozen and committed before the held-out run.
baseline_evidence: No Sanctuary work on change ringing or shuffling (grep of LEARNING). Background from memory, not relied on: adjacent-transposition shuffles mix in order n^3 log n. Whether the parallel variant is studied in the literature was not checked, so broader novelty is not claimed. The association is generative provenance; the hypothesis is tested on its own merits, with no ablation of the analogy required.
experiment: Discovery note; register; write exact evaluator; dev gate n=4..6; freeze; held-out n=7,8; assess.
score_basis: Provisional estimates, not measured ROI. Leverage 1: curiosity only. Depth 2: exact finite computation on a parallel-move shuffle. Cost 0.1: stdlib CPU, no model calls. Friction 1. Priority = (1x2)/(0.1x1) = 20.
strategic_intent: Associative cross-domain discovery practice that ends in a decidable finite computation.
design_constraints: Exact finite result for n<=8 only; no asymptotic claim
The random-change chain borrows ringing's move set but not its no-repeat rule
